Our Mission · Why This Paper Exists

A newspaper that studies with you

Every morning, somewhere in India — in a rented room in Delhi, a library in Kochi, a bus in Patna, a village veranda in Vidarbha — an aspirant opens this paper and begins the oldest ritual of this examination: reading the day and asking what it means. Open - News exists to do that reading honestly. We take the week’s events, cross-check them against primary documents and at least one reputable second source, and then write them the way a good writer would — as stories, not notes. The syllabus is woven into the narration; the keywords are set in bold so a second glance becomes a revision; and nothing is padded, because your attention is the only price we charge.

Our mission is simple to state and hard to do: make one Sunday of reading do the work of a week of coaching. We do not summarise other people’s summaries. We do not sell fear, ranks, or shortcuts. We write the news the way the Examiner reads it — for its concepts, its linkages, and its consequences — and we trust you to do the rest. Instead of handing you the fish, we teach the water.

“One paper. One hour. No barriers of city, class, or coaching fee.”The Open - News promise
Our Vision · The Long Game

We imagine an India where the distance between a district town and a Delhi coaching hub is zero pages wide. Where the daughter of a farmer and the son of a professor open the same paper, at the same hour, with the same chance. This is a national paper with no home city and no favourite region: the floods of the Himalaya, the fields of the Deccan, the courts of the capital and the fishing villages of the coast all report to the same front page. If the civil service is meant to belong to all of India, then the reading that leads to it must belong to all of India first.

Why Open Source · A Heritage, Not A Product

Knowledge that refuses to be owned

India’s deepest tradition is not secrecy — it is transmission. The Vedas survived a thousand years without copyright, carried mouth to mouth because someone decided knowledge was a duty owed forward. Nalanda and Takshashila took students from every direction and asked their questions, not their origins. When humanity has been at its best — the library, the printing press, the public university, the open internet — it has been because someone chose to give understanding away.

Open - News stands in that line. It is open source because the news of a republic belongs to the citizens of that republic; because an aspirant’s poverty should decide nothing about an aspirant’s preparation; and because every generation must leave the next one a fuller shelf than it found. Take this paper, share it, print it, translate it, archive it. It was never ours to lock away — and it is not yours to lock away either.

A step for the future of India

Every administrator this country will have in 2050 is, today, a reader somewhere. What they read now — how carefully, how honestly, how widely — will quietly decide how they govern later. We think of each edition as a small act of nation-building: not a headline shouted, but a habit of mind handed over. If even one future officer learns from these pages to check the source, to see the linkage, to respect the citizen at the end of every policy — the paper has done its work.

How every edition is made

Primary document first. Judgments, gazettes, official releases — before anyone’s opinion of them.

Two-source cross-check. No fact enters the paper on one witness.

Narration in service of memory. Stories, because the mind keeps stories longer than lists.

Keywords in bold. Your revision layer, laid inline. Read twice: once for the story, once for the bold.

Credits · Permanent Acknowledgement of Sources

Where the news comes from

Every edition of Open - News is researched from, and cross-checked against, the public reporting and official publications of the following. They do the first and hardest work of journalism and public record; we gratefully acknowledge it. This list is a permanent fixture of this page.

  • Official & Primary
  • Press Information Bureau (PIB), Government of India
  • Supreme Court of India — judgments & cause lists
  • The Gazette of India & ministry notifications
  • Reserve Bank of India — bulletins & reports
  • Election Commission of India
  • NDMA, ISRO, FSSAI, NMC & other statutory bodies
  • Indian Press
  • The Hindu
  • The Indian Express
  • PRS Legislative Research
  • Drishti IAS, ForumIAS, Shankar IAS, Legacy IAS — weekly compilations
  • Other credited Indian dailies & wire services (PTI, ANI)
  • Getty Images, AP & credited photographers — imagery
  • Global & Multilateral
  • United Nations bodies (UNCCD, WHO, UN treaty bodies)
  • Associated Press (AP) & international wires
  • ICIMOD & scientific institutions as cited
  • World Bank, IMF & rating agencies as cited
  • Typefaces: Chomsky, PT Serif, Playfair Display, Oswald (open licences)
